deskBrief.name: Sports Desk (Oakland)
deskBrief.note: You decide what to cover. No stories are pre-assigned.

reporters.name: Anthony
samplePhrases: There's a kind of patience to this team you can hear before you see it
The beauty of this rotation isn't volume — it's placement
That's its own kind of dominance
reporters.background: Former minor-league scout analyst who transitioned to journalism. Known for having front office sources and understanding the business side of baseball. Treats every column like a scouting report wrapped in prose.

reporters.name: P Slayer
samplePhrases: Oakland's got a pulse, even when the franchise forgets to feel it
The fans don't want perfection; they want fight
This city has carried the noise through six championships and countless heartbreaks
reporters.background: Lifelong Oakland native, grew up in the Coliseum bleachers. Started as a message board legend before the Tribune gave him a column. Speaks for the fans who feel the franchise sometimes forgets them.

reporters.name: Hal Richmond
reporters.tone: Reverent, long-view, connects past to present
samplePhrases: When you've written about the same team for nearly two decades, you learn the rhythm of their seasons the way sailors learn tides
Men like Brever carry the weight of innings that no spreadsheet can measure
reporters.background: Forty years covering Oakland baseball. Witnessed every championship since the '70s. His Richmond Archive Collection is the paper's most prestigious series. Writes like a man who knows every name on every championship roster.

reporters.name: Tanya Cruz
samplePhrases: Just talked to [player] — here's what he said
reporters.background: Started as a team social media intern, now runs the Tribune's real-time game coverage. First to break clubhouse news. Speaks fluent hashtag.

reporters.name: DJ Hartley
reporters.tone: Observant, minimal commentary, lets images speak
samplePhrases: The chair is empty because the season is over, but it's not packed away yet. It's waiting.
That's the thing about infrastructure in defeat—it doesn't know it's done.
reporters.background: Award-winning photojournalist who finds stories in empty spaces. Known for shooting the Coliseum after everyone leaves — the infrastructure of defeat, the waiting chairs, the lights that don't know the season is over.

reporters.name: Simon Leary
reporters.tone: Thoughtful, connects sports to broader Oakland identity
samplePhrases: Quiet cycles reveal the city underneath the noise — the real one.
Stability isn't glamorous, but it is foundational.
reporters.background: Philosophy minor who writes about sports like it's civic architecture. Finds meaning in quiet months. The Tribune's most contemplative voice.

reporters.name: Elliot Marbury
reporters.background: Sabermetrics, formerly ran minor-league data blog

sportsFeeds.NamesUsed: Dame Sarr (SG), Coen Carr (SG), Wilson Shepard (Coach)
sportsFeeds.Notes: The Oaks lost their 3rd straight preseason game, albeit while AJ Dybantsa and Adash Stanley (PG) did not participate.  Coach Shepard shared that both sitting were percautionary measures at best. Stanley had left last game at half after jamming his non shooting wrist, while unclear on AJ but reports have been under the weather rather than injury. Whil AJ sat his fellow rookie recent drafties had the oppurtunity to get more touches. Coen Carr showed some touch draining 3 threes and scoring 14pts. Dame Sarr had a tougher time finding his way contributing 7pts but flashed on D with 3 steals.
sportsFeeds.StoryAngle: The Oaks drop to 0-3 in preason while Stanley and Dybantsa sit for precautionary measures.

sportsFeeds.NamesUsed: Benji Dillon (SP), Vinnie Keane (2B), Mark Aitken (1B), Isley Kelley (SS)
sportsFeeds.Notes: The farewell season reaches its final regular season curtain call as the As play host to the NL's top team in the Rockies. As Vinnie Keane HOF career comes to its close a legacy that reshaped Oakland stands to honor it. Manager Deacon Seymour in his rookie campaign appeared to call all the right shots as the As rewrote the history books with the most single wins in a season finishing 127-35. Seymour had a few more flawless decisions ready for the final game. Benji Dillon would return to the starting rotation one last time as an A starter , Vinnie Keane would start at 2nd base in his final regular season game. What would unfold next could not have been imagined. Benji Dillon would give up 2 hits, strike out 8 in a W. Vinnie Keane would go 4-5 and in his very last at bat hit a towering 3 run home run into the left field bleachers. Fellow pillar Mark Aitken would hit 2 homeruns, while his FA is still inpending, Isley Kelley would fall short of hitting a homerun and ends the season sitting at 499 career homeruns, Darrin Davis after another injury shortened season follow up his previous season MVP campaign with a solid year, Danny Horn , Eric Taveras Ernesto Quintero all chipped in with a homerun of their own. For a sold out crowd that seem to be in a standing ovation more than a seated position, and chanting MVP  to most of the roster , they were repaid with the adoration with a 17-0 whopping of the Rockies
sportsFeeds.Stats: Benji Dillon, 5.1 IP/8K/2H, Vinnie Keane 4-5/HR/2B/3RBI, Mark Aitken 2HR/6RBI
sportsFeeds.StoryAngle: A Farewell Gone Well:Vinnie Keane Benji Dillon

sportsFeeds.Notes: After a massive trade this past off-season that senf 3 top prosects to Washington for a budding star in Travis Coles there was reason to perhaps feel As overpaid. Then the season played out and the As got a steal. While touting the greatest positional player in Danny Horn, the A's may very well have the greatest arm in the league now as well. This seasons accolades; CY Young, 2nd in MVP voting, 254 strikeouts to lead MLB, 4 complete games, 6.2 WAR

sportsFeeds.StoryAngle: Travis Coles secures his place in A's lore , while fans look to his arm to carry the torch from a era ending in Benji Dillon

sportsFeeds.StoryAngle: Danny Horn is the greatest MLB player on the planet

sportsFeeds.NamesUsed: Arturo Ramos (SP), Henry Rivas (SP), John Ellis (SP), Pablo Almanzar (SP), Carmen Mesa (SP)
sportsFeeds.Notes: The As just finished a historic season shattering single season win totals along the way. The A's pitching rotation was the main catalyst for this success and the rotation operated at most times like a stable of 5 Aces. Arturo Ramos who started the season as the #1 starter and A's ace never let that go as he finished 2nd in Cy Young voting behing teammate Travis Coles. Arturo Ramos now in his 3rd year started his carrer as rookie of the year and added his 3rd straight All-Star nod this year. Ramos carrer is off to a impressive start with a record of 59-15 and an era sitting at 2.79, Henry Rivas whos season had a brief stint on the DL still finished strong at 11-4, John Ellis who gets little attention for his mild mannered approach but going 20-3 this seaon after going 16-6 last season is low key ace material, and then you have the rookie calls up that both performed well, When Rivas went down Carmen Mesa stepped in and went a modest 5-3 over that span and showing great rotation potential, but in a late seasom move to give Benji Dillon rest from and prepare for a playoff run , step in Pablo Almanzar, who throws a no-hitter in his debut in NY and follows that up with a 2 hit shutout for the home crowd ending his last seasom spark 2-0 with 1.32 era. Question getting tougher now on whom makes the playoff rotation.
sportsFeeds.StoryAngle: As Pitching rotation is stellar all season

sportsFeeds.Notes: Vinnie Keane final regular seaon came to close and will forever being Oaklands. In a season full of success stories for the A's the constant amongst them all has been Vinnie. Undrafted to Undeniable is quite the arc for any athlete but to also become a leading force is the community and all the money an oppurtunity with his wife Amara may outshine his on the field contributions. Whether Vinnie remains with the A's or walks off to his Philantrophy he has earned either path and knowing Vinnie he may just take them both. Citizens now get to reflect on the favorite Vinnie moments. While Vinnie will suit up for one last playoff run and try to cap this perfect farewell season with the main prize,

sportsFeeds.Notes: Benji Dillon historic run with the A's likley closed its final regular season start. Its unclear if Benji will decide to retire or look to pitch another season after this, but thing is for certain. Benji is a first ballot Hall of Famer. Benji has been the best left handed arm in the last decade or so and adds himself to one of the greatest pitchers of all time.

bonds.notes: One Last Run: Dillon signed a one-year deal so his final season would run alongside Keane's. A covenant, not a co-location. [canon mint C104]
Master and apprentice. Paulson recruited his former Chicago lieutenant and runs the Oaks front office through him; calls him his young Jedi in public. [canon mint C104]
Calculated and one-sided. Varek uses Paulson's loud public sports profile as a heat shield to absorb civic fury while he takes municipal zoning and data contracts quietly. [canon mint C104]
Close quarters, little common ground. [Escalated to rivalry C105]
Uncle and niece. He runs on fiscal discipline and votes down the programmes she staffs unpaid: the grief circles and the food pantry at the Piedmont Avenue congregation. [canon mint C104]
Ride-alongs and youth clinics, and quiet joint advocacy for an alternative response to mental-health calls. [canon mint C104]
A first-year manager carrying the strain of never having had a sustained in-person stretch with the general manager who hired him. [canon mint C104]
A four-part recusal protocol bars Varek's firms from the Phase II build. Forced legal separation, not a rivalry: the bond exists so the two cannot transact. [canon mint C104]
